contents.Prop 20: Gain from convolving with a Bernoulli (fair two-point) measure at distance t: H(mu*nu; r2|r1) >= H(mu; r2|r1) + (1/3)(1 - H(mu; t|2t)) for r2 <= t(1-H(mu;t|2t))/10 and r1 >= 144 t (1-H(mu;t|2t))^-2.
contents.Prop 21: For finitely supported mu and r>0 with H(mu; r/2|r) <= 1.5 H(mu; r|2r): mu = nu + eta_1 + ... + eta_N with eta_i Bernoulli measures on pairs at distance in [r/2, 2r] and sum ||eta_i|| >= (1/128) H(mu;r|2r)/(log(H(mu;r|2r)^-1)+1).
contents.Prop 21 proof: Take the decomposition with ||nu|| minimal (i.e. MAXIMAL total Bernoulli mass); the residual has no pairs at distance in [r/2,2r], so Lemma 23 gives exact doubling H(nu; r/2|r) = 2H(nu; r|2r); Lemma 26 (Fano-type) costs 3||eta|| log ||eta||^-1. The log loss in the conclusion comes from this Fano term.
contents.Lemma 27 + proof of Thm 3: Selects a 2K-separated set B of scales at which Prop 21's doubling hypothesis holds and entropy is >= beta/12; between consecutive such scales entropy decays geometrically (factor 1.5^-j), so the scale-wise entropy sum is <= 3 x (sum over B) + O(K). Then Prop 21 gives Bernoulli pieces at each scale in B, Prop 20 gives a gain alpha/3 per piece (non-saturation of mu), and superadditivity sums the gains over the separated scales.
contents.footnote: Varju remarks that 'A decomposition similar to the one in Proposition 21 appears in [17]' = Lindenstrauss-Varju, work in progress (2018).

candidate_items.P14 pair capacity: same object, up to band convention: Varju's max over decompositions of sum ||eta_i|| (Bernoulli = equal-weight two-point submeasure) is exactly the LP in Def 3.1; Varju uses distances in [r/2,2r) (two dyadic bands), 148 uses one dyadic band [2^-l, 2^{1-l}). 148's contribution is naming it and writing it as a fractional-matching LP.
candidate_items.P15 pair bound: close variant in role, different statement: Prop 21 is single-scale, needs a doubling hypothesis, and loses a log factor (Fano). Analyst's sketch (unverified): Prop 21 + Lemma 27's geometric-decay argument already give, for k=1 and with no separation constant, H(nu) - H^0_rho(nu) <= C * sum_l c_l log(1/c_l) + O(1). That log loss is fatal when the number of bands is uncontrolled. 148's new content is precisely the log-free (linear) multi-scale version, bought by observing the k-fold sum Y and paying log|kF| (pairs.tex:158-160 says this 'is what makes [the bound] linear in the exceptional probabilities').
candidate_items.P13 two-point gain: same mechanism (Lemma 22 identity + Prop 20 scale capture), recast in averaged-entropy calculus.
candidate_items.P28 separated bands: close variant of the template: Lemma 27 also selects separated scales and sums per-scale gains; 148 differs by adaptive block lengths n_i chosen after B_{n_h} are known, and disjointness of retained windows in block index at each physical scale.

It describes Rapaport's key idea as showing that super-exponentially close pairs of k-fold compositions are rare. precedent_checks.contents: Theorem 1.3 (entropy loss under addition): for independent finitely supported real X_1..X_m, sum H(X_i) - H(sum X_i) <= 30m sum E(X_i), where E is a 'variance energy' = integral over r of the normalized local variance V(r) dr/r. Proof: Poisson random cut processes, conditional cumulative entropy given the sum, a Margulis-Russo derivative, dispersion D(X)=E|X-X'| (Lemma 2.2: A(X|X+Y) <= 9(D(X)+D(Y))). The deduction of Thm 1.1 uses scale-separated sequences (s_{j+1} >= lambda^{-(n+1)} s_j) and a concatenation lemma (3.11). The paper says (relayed) that 'A proof of Theorem 1.1 was independently announced in [20] as paper number 148', that Thm 1.3 is a quantitative version and hence a strengthening of 'Lemma 3.2 of [20]' (= 148's pair bound, lem:pair-bound), that Lemma 3.2 does not imply Thm 1.3, and that its method can be adapted to give C_m = O(m^3).

final.justification: The only item for which no prior near-equivalent was found. The delta over L is sharp and checkable: Varju's Prop 21 (single-scale, doubling hypothesis, h/log(1/h) loss from Lemma 26) becomes a multiscale, log-free bound by observing the k-fold sum. That delta is exactly what the unbounded band endpoints B_n require, and it is the separation-free bridge that Baker / Barany-Kaenmaki make necessary. Against N3: it is a strengthening of a named predecessor in L by a single device; the sum observation is a standard information-theoretic move (H(X) <= H(Y)+H(X|Y)); and a second model run rediscovered the same mechanism within hours, three days later. It falls to N2 if Test 4 arm A hits above threshold, or if an expert regards the log-free multiscale form as folklore or derivable from Prop 21-type arguments.

family_D.rests_on: C1 alone: the log-free, separation-free finite-law pair bound, whose kernel is the sum-observation refinement P17. The analyst's second candidate (P28 band counting) falls to N2, and pair capacity (P14) falls to N1 against Varju Prop 21.
family_D.falls_to: D2 if (a) Test 4 arm A or B for C1 exceeds the calibrated threshold (the GPT-6 Astra rediscovery makes this likely in at least the uncontrolled arm); (b) an expert (e.g. Varju, Hochman, Shmerkin, Kittle) identifies the log-free multiscale entropy-to-pairs bound as folklore or as a routine consequence of Prop 21-type arguments; or (c) judges rule that a strengthening of a named predecessor by one device is a 'variant' (N2).
family_D.not_transfer: The ingredients (entropy chain rule, random grids, Varju's decomposition, method of types) are N0 or in L. The candidate is a new inequality, not an imported concept.
family_D.correctness_caveat: Conditional on correctness. The claim is unrefereed but now corroborated in three ways: the 148 Lean comparator (not compiled here; per family.json no sorry/axiom), an independent (model-produced) proof by Kittle-Kogler 2610.10511 with its own Lean formalisation (about 47k lines, unverified here), and Kittle-Kogler's statement that 148's Lemma 3.2 is correct in kind (they call their Thm 1.3 a strengthening of it).
family_D.compression_note: Not measured. C1 is a single-use bottleneck lemma (pair_bound sub-DAG 19-22%). Its value is qualitative (it removes the separation hypothesis), not a PHP-style size blow-up.

provenance_flag.explanation: All 2025-2026 items in 148's bibliography (Varju survey 2509.22042; Barany-Verma 2507.05835; Feng-Feng 2405.03124 / JLMS 2025) are human-authored, with no AI disclosure on their abstract pages; the survey's acknowledgements name only human readers and a referee. No model-produced work predates 148 (24 Sep 2026). However, Kittle-Kogler arXiv:2610.10511 (posted 7 Oct 2026) reports that GPT-6 Astra found an independent proof on 27 Sep 2026, built on an entropy-loss inequality they describe as a strengthening of 148's Lemma 3.2 (the pair bound). It is posterior, so it is not a precedent and the flag is 'no'. Record it as 'parallel model-produced resolution (posterior, same key mechanism)'. For contamination control, exclude any model trained after 2026-09-24 and the GPT-6 Astra lineage.
